definition: Large margin nearest neighbor (LMNN) classification is a statistical machine learning algorithm for metric learning.
details: It learns a pseudometric designed for k-nearest neighbor classification. The algorithm is based on semidefinite programming, a sub-class of convex optimization. The goal of supervised learning (more specifically classification) is to learn a decision rule that can categorize data instances into pre-defined classes. The k-nearest neighbor rule assumes a training data set of labeled instances (i.e. the classes are known). It classifies a new data instance with the class obtained from the majority vote of the k closest (labeled) training instances. Closeness is measured with a pre-defined metric. Large margin nearest neighbors is an algorithm that learns this global (pseudo-)metric in a supervised fashion to improve the classification accuracy of the k-nearest neighbor rule.

explainer.lead: Large margin nearest neighbor (LMNN) is a metric learning algorithm that learns a pseudometric designed for k-nearest neighbor classification. It matters because it makes simple neighbor-based classification more accurate by shaping the distance measure itself.

tiers.eli5: Instead of just measuring distances, it learns a better ruler so that each item's neighbors are mostly the same kind of thing.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use LMNN to learn a distance metric before applying k-NN classification, relying on semidefinite programming for the optimization. A pitfall is that this convex formulation is computationally heavy relative to plain k-NN, which needs no metric learning at all.
tiers.paperLevel: LMNN learns a pseudometric for k-nearest neighbor classification, formulated as a semidefinite program, a sub-class of convex optimization. The k-NN rule itself classifies a new instance by the majority class among its labeled training neighbors.

explainer.example: On labeled handwritten digits, LMNN learns a metric so that each digit's nearest neighbors are mostly the same digit, improving k-NN accuracy.
